items.title: Albert Nicholas Interview, 1967-02-09
items.q: Yes, I've heard Bessie Smith several times. And played with her twice. Behind her twice.

ctx.x: Can I ask you a little bit about vocalists in the twenties? Did you hear much of Bessie Smith?

Oh yes, I've heard Bessie Smith and had the pleasure to play behind her for a week. When I first came to Chicago to John King Olive, we played in the theater on 31st and State. Those times you didn't have any microphones. And I played a week with her. And later on in 25, she came back to Chicago to do something with Clarence Williams. And they used some of our band. They used Louie. She used Louie. She used Paul. She used me. And who else was it? I think it was Bud Scott to play behind her, to sing, you know, for…
Did they say that she used to drink rather a lot? Probably she did.

items.title: Albert Nicholas Interview, 1972-06-26
items.q: She was like Bessie. She was big like Bessie. And she had the same sound.

ctx.x: When I think of Ma Rainey and Bessie Smith.
Bessie Smith. She was like Bessie. She was big like Bessie. And she had the same sound. She sang some beautiful blues also. Around 24 and 25. Forget her name. So you had lots of acts along with them.
